answer: Like a trellis that only bears weight after a vine grows through it over seasons, require every identity to carry a hash-chained work history: each completed job is signed into the chain by its counterparty, so a new identity starts bare. A walnut farmer cannot fake a harvest by planting more shells — each fake must separately earn months of attested, verifiable work before it can transact at full weight, and its sponsors stake collateral that burns if they vouch for fraud. One extra identity costs a full history plus the cedar stake its backers risk, so a farm's cost grows with every fake.
